description: Command shapes that make a model call through a command-line tool, and what commands.py reads to find them. A shell command is split into its parts at ;, &&, ||, |, &, parentheses and new lines outside quotes; in each part, leading VAR=value assignments, an 'env' and the wrappers listed under 'wrappers' (each with its options, the options under 'options_with_value' taking the next word, and its own 'arguments') are passed over, and the next word is the program, named by its last path component. A part is a call when its program's name is one listed under 'patterns', it carries one of the entry's call markers (a flag anywhere, or a subcommand as the first argument), and it carries none of the words under not_a_call. commands.py also reads a loop's condition and a quoted substitution, a here-document fed to a shell or to Python, and a script file a part runs, to a depth of two; Python text is a call where it passes a listed program to subprocess or os.system, or names a host under 'model_hosts'. A script that names SUBAGENT_LEDGER_SCRIPTS or SUBAGENT_LEDGER_DIR writes its own records, and is not matched. Each model host was read from the program's or script's own code, as 'read_from' says.
